question: What would you suspect in a patient who has difficulty in laterally raising the arm (limitation of arm abduction from 30 degrees) and paresthesias in the lateral portion of the shoulder, without pain, and that the previous day has suffered a dislocation escapulohumeral?

options.opb: A lesion of the axillary nerve (circumflex).
options.opc: An injury of the musculocutaneous nerve.
options.opd: A rupture of the scapulohumeral ligaments.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Dislocation escapulohumeral" -> "Axillary nerve injury" -> "Difficulty in arm abduction from 30 degrees" -> "Paresthesias in lateral shoulder" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Dislocation escapulohumeral" -> "Radial nerve injury" -> "Possible wrist drop" -> "Unlikely cause of shoulder symptoms" -> 30%
CHAIN: "Dislocation escapulohumeral" -> "Musculocutaneous nerve injury" -> "Weakness in elbow flexion" -> "Unlikely cause of shoulder symptoms" -> 25%
CHAIN: "Dislocation escapulohumeral" -> "Rupture of scapulohumeral ligaments" -> "Possible instability" -> "No paresthesias" -> 40%
analysis: The symptoms described are consistent with an axillary nerve injury. The axillary nerve innervates the deltoid muscle, which is responsible for abducting the arm beyond 15-30 degrees. It also provides sensation to the lateral portion of the shoulder. The history of a shoulder dislocation is a common cause of axillary nerve injury.
